report.what: Pre-registered test-set evaluation (P16): four configurations, each run once.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.what: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor reads each page once; every value is accepted

A.label: Archivist, arm A (headline)
A.what: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor reads every value in context and again in isolation, the documents' own checks, SAM 3.1 occlusion; policy v2

B.label: Archivist, arm B (all open weights)
B.what: Muse Spark Open on Baseten for the extraction and both reads, the documents' own checks, SAM 3.1 occlusion; policy v2

C.label: Archivist, arm C (two models)
C.what: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor reads in context, Muse Spark Open re-reads in isolation, the documents' own checks, SAM 3.1 occlusion; policy v2

H1.claim: The headline's error rate among accepted fields is lower than the baseline's, with non-overlapping 95% intervals.
H1.summary: Archivist (arm A) accepted 3330 values and 12 were wrong: 0.36% (95% interval 0.14% to 0.67%). The baseline accepted 4251 values and 189 were wrong: 4.45% (95% interval 2.28% to 7.14%). Archivist's rate is lower and the intervals do not overlap.

H2.claim: The headline catches at least 85% of wrong values.
H2.summary: Of 189 wrong values, Archivist (arm A) sent 177 to review: 93.65% (95% interval 88.31% to 97.28%). The threshold is 85% or more.

H3.claim: The headline sends at most 20% of fields to review.
H3.summary: Archivist (arm A) sent 921 of 4267 fields to review: 21.58% (95% interval 15.44% to 27.87%). The threshold is 20% or less.

H4.claim: The all-open-weights arm's error rate among accepted fields is below 1%.
H4.summary: Arm B accepted 3296 values and 10 were wrong: 0.30% (95% interval 0.12% to 0.54%). The threshold is below 1%, judged on the rate itself.

H5.claim: The headline flags at least 90% of the planted source errors.
H5.summary: Archivist (arm A) sent a field of 23 of 26 planted source errors to review: 88.46%. The threshold is 90% or more.

notes: One run of each configuration on one synthetic test set: 157 pages from 12 accounts, with source errors planted at a fixed rate. Real archives will differ.
The intervals resample pages as if they were independent, as pre-registered. Pages of one account share names, amounts and balances, so they are not, and the intervals may understate the uncertainty.
The headline (arm A, policy v2) was chosen on dev and val before the test set was run (D29). The test set decided nothing.

Error rate among accepted fields counts every accepted value that is not the printed one, including values accepted as blank. A page that failed to extract scores all its fields as omitted: they count as wrong values nobody caught, and are not accepted.

False alarms are correct values sent to review, not counting the fields of a planted source error, where a flag is a find. A source error counts as found when any of its fields is sent to review; the report does not check the reason given.

Classification and citation accuracy belong to the extraction run, so the arms that verify the same extraction share them. Citation accuracy is the share of correct values whose box has its centre inside the printed value's box.

Cost per page is computed from the price lists in the configs, not from invoices. Muse Spark 1.3 runs at Contributor prices (D19). Muse Spark Open's prices are the figures Baseten's marketing page prints, which is not a contract. Cached input is billed as ordinary input, so cost is overstated, never understated.

Arm B extracts with a different model, so its error rate measures the whole configuration, not the verification alone. The table "What each arm's extraction would have let in without verification" shows what each arm's extraction run would have accepted on its own.
